q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 23, 2026. This is a 3-day window until the actual announcement. The resolution is essentially immediate.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has provided **explicit forward guidance** for Q2 FY2027 revenue: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.18 billion to $92.82 billion**.

This is not a prediction about an uncertain future event—NVIDIA has already made this guidance public (on May 20, 2026, per the research). The company is legally bound by SEC regulations to issue revenue guidance before the quarter ends, and they have done so.

Wall Street's consensus estimate sits at approximately **$91.9 billion**, near the midpoint of the guidance range. Historical context shows Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, representing strong sequential growth (+20%), and year-over-year acceleration (85%). The sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 (guidance midpoint) would be approximately 11.5%, which is modest but reasonable for a mature, high-revenue company.

**The most likely outcome is that the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue will fall within or very close to NVIDIA's guided range of $89.18–$92.82 billion, with central tendency near $91.0 billion.**

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Demand weakness**: Unexpected softness in data center spending (though no evidence of this appears in the research)
- **China revenue deterioration**: Further impacts from U.S. licensing restrictions on H20 chips (already excluded from guidance since April 2025)
- **Manufacturing/supply constraints**: Unexpected production issues limiting shipments
- **Macro deterioration**: Sudden economic downturn dampening customer demand
- **Guidance miss to the downside**: NVIDIA coming in below their own $89.18B floor (rare for guided quarters, but possible)

The company would need to miss its own low-end guidance significantly for the result to fall substantially below $89 billion. This is uncommon unless a major unexpected event occurs.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Demand upside**: Stronger-than-expected AI/data center adoption, particularly from enterprise customers
- **Pricing strength**: Customers willing to pay premium pricing for scarce GPU capacity
- **Geographic diversification**: Expansion outside U.S.-restricted markets if licensing changes favorably
- **Product mix shift**: Higher-margin products outperforming expectations
- **Guidance beat**: NVIDIA exceeding the high end of their $92.82B range (possible but less common—companies typically guide conservatively)

The upper bound of the range ($92.82B) represents a modest beat scenario. Breaking significantly above this would require demand to exceed what NVIDIA's own planning suggests is reasonable.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 revenue**: $81.6 billion (up 20% sequentially, 85% year-over-year)
- **Year-ago quarter (Q2 FY2026) revenue**: $46.7 billion (implying near-doubling YoY at guidance midpoint)
- **Wall Street consensus**: $91.9 billion
- **NVIDIA's formal guidance**: $91.0 billion ± 2% ($89.18–$92.82 billion)

When a public company issues formal quarterly guidance (which is legally and reputationally binding), actual results typically fall within that range approximately 85–90% of the time for mature, established companies like NVIDIA. Misses outside the guidance range are notable and material events.

---

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

Given that:
1. NVIDIA has provided **explicit, formal guidance** (not an estimate but a commitment)
2. The earnings release occurs in **3 days** (resolution is imminent)
3. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) sits near the midpoint, suggesting no major surprises are priced in
4. No recent research suggests NVIDIA will miss its own guidance significantly
5. Historical accuracy for NVIDIA's guidance is generally high

The distribution should be **tightly concentrated around the guided range**, with slight skew toward the midpoint:

- **10th percentile (Low)**: ~$88.5 billion (below low end of guidance but not catastrophically)
- **50th percentile (Median)**: ~$91.0 billion (midpoint of guidance)
- **90th percentile (High)**: ~$93.2 billion (modestly above high end of guidance)

The guided range is $89.18–$92.82B. I'll place my distribution slightly wider than the formal guidance range to account for the small but non-zero probability of NVIDIA missing its own guidance in either direction.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China, a policy in place since April 2025 due to U.S. licensing requirements for H20 chips [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range. This suggests a modest beat, with the top end of NVIDIA's guidance reaching $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The year-ago quarter saw revenue of $46.7 billion, implying a near-doubling of revenue year-over-year at the midpoint of the guidance [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, up 20% sequentially and 85% year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The company will release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).
